subject: conditionalPanel and shiny module not working together?

messages.author: e2d55149db2af418
messages.subject: conditionalPanel and shiny module not working together?
parts:
Dear Shiny developers of conditionalPanel and shiny module, I could be wrong but it seems these two features don't work together as expected.

The following code work just fine as itself on any ui.R, the two buttons are displayed as expected

      selectizeInput(
        'mySelect', 'Test Select', choices = state.name,
        options = list(
          placeholder = 'Please select an option below',
          onInitialize = I('function() { this.setValue(""); }')
        )
      ),
      conditionalPanel("input.mySelect == 'Alabama' ", actionButton("go1", "Go Button1")),
      conditionalPanel("input.mySelect != ''", actionButton("go2", "Go Button2"))


However, if I put them inside a module such as following, the buttons are displayed not based on the conditions.
I am not sure where the ns should be placed so I tried both ns('input.mySelect') or input.ns('mySelect'), neither worked.

testUI <- function(id, label = "CSV file") {
  # Create a namespace function using the provided id
  ns <- NS(id)
  
  tagList(wellPanel(
    fileInput(ns("file"), label),
    checkboxInput(ns("heading"), "Has heading"),
    selectInput(ns("quote"), "Quote", c(
      "None" = "",
      "Double quote" = "\"",
      "Single quote" = "'"
    ))),
    conditionalPanel(!is.null(ns("file")),
      actionButton("go1", label="Go Button1", icon = NULL)
    ),
    selectizeInput(
      ns("mySelect"), "Test Select", choices = state.name,
      options = list(
        placeholder = "Please select an option below",
        onInitialize = I('function() { this.setValue(""); }')
      )
    ),
    conditionalPanel("input.ns('mySelect') == 'Alabama' ", actionButton("go2", "Go Button2")),
    conditionalPanel("ns('input.mySelect') != ''", actionButton("go3", "Go Button3")),
    dataTableOutput(ns("table"))
  )
}


Any insight is greatly appreciated.

-Jian

messages.author: ebed243cfaa1e3bb
messages.subject: Re: conditionalPanel and shiny module not working together?
parts:
You're on the right track, but the string you give to conditionalPanel is meant to be evaluated by JavaScript, and the ns() function is for R.  You need to construct the condition statement in R so that it uses the value returned by ns().

Instead of
"input.mySelect == 'Alabama' "


you should use
paste0("input['",
       ns("mySelect"),
       "'] == 'Alabama' ")

And all other JavaScript statements in the module should build the names of input variables in a similar way.


Here's the (slightly smaller) example of this solution I made with your code:

testUI <- function(id, label = "CSV file") {
  # Create a namespace function using the provided id
  ns <- NS(id)
 
  tagList(

selectizeInput(
      ns('mySelect'), 'Test Select', choices = state.name,
      options = list(
        placeholder = 'Please select an option below',
        onInitialize = I('function() { this.setValue(""); }')
      )
    ),
conditionalPanel(paste0("input['", ns("mySelect"), "'] == 'Alabama' "),
actionButton("go1", "Go Button1")),
conditionalPanel(paste0("input['", ns("mySelect"), "'] != ''"),
actionButton("go2", "Go Button2"))

)
}

new_ui <- shinyUI(
  fluidPage(
    testUI('myNamespace')
  )
)

server <- shinyServer(function(input, output) {})

runApp(appDir = list(ui = new_ui, server = server))

Joe,

Just a heads up, this syntax doesn't seem to work. The panel will always show.
sprintf("input.%s != ''", ns("mySelect"))

It looks like you need to use:
sprintf("input['%s'] != ''", ns("mySelect"))

gist: https://gist.github.com/tbadams45/49c71a4314f6b4f299583f4ba96fee54
